rules: Bound source bytes/count and serialized snapshot bytes before starting the compiler process.

Count raw stdout bytes and bound each frame before UTF-8 decoding and JSON parsing. Legacy and direct non-declaration sessions, including explicit Canonical psc-checked-seed-products/2 sessions, allow two frames; explicitly selected psc-checked-seed-products/1 declaration sessions allow exactly one additional writer response.
Bound diagnostics, admissions before checker invocation and total emitted source/IR bytes before returning a successful session.

Each asynchronous protocol/checker wait has a phase timeout. Kill the selected compiler child on failure and confirm its close before removing temporary inputs; unconfirmed termination is infrastructureUnavailable.

Preserve prepared -> trusted checker acceptance -> emit/checked. Direct declaration requests remain in the same native prepared session after exact staged-subject checks; any limit/failure aborts without successful data.
Bind configured native session limits and whole-session observations into affected pass records, explicitly without per-pass resource attribution.
limitations: Trusted host event loop: a synchronous in-process checker cannot be preempted by a timer.
A timed-out asynchronous checker may finish later, but its result cannot authorize emission in this failed session.
Limits describe protocol bytes and asynchronous waiting, not process CPU, peak memory, descendants, compiler-internal work or host stack.
No malicious-host sandbox, global resource monotonicity theorem or preservation theorem follows.
